images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of StreamVibe.(a) StreamVibe studies sustained proactive interaction under explicit, implicit, and dynamically evolving user intents, where the agent continuously observes the environment and decides when and how to assist. (b) Existing paradigms rely on explicit intents, with limited tracking of interaction state and evolving intents. StreamVibe addresses these limitations through proactive streaming policy learning and persistent interaction state modeling that tracks task progress and updates active intents.

Figure 2:Construction and statistics of StreamVibe-Bench.(a) Data construction from task videos and user context to evidence annotation, human verification, and causal stream generation.
(b) Sample allocation across three requirement types, with examples from physical and digital environments.
(c) Pointwise and trajectory evaluation settings for local response decisions and continuous interaction behavior. TP: true positives; FP: false positives; FN: false negatives.
(d) Joint distribution of video duration, sample count, and average number of evidence points per sample.

Figure 3:Overview of StreamVibe.(a) During inference, StreamVibe-Harness maintains persistent interaction state, tracks each intent through an independent lifecycle, and retrieves relevant history from hierarchical memory, providing StreamVibe-VL with a unified context for response decisions. (b) Adaptive streaming SFT balances wait/speak decisions and jointly supervises timing and content. (c) Localized trajectory RL samples causal rollouts around help points, combining point-level timing and content rewards with trajectory-level rewards on coverage, density, order, consistency, and redundancy.

Figure 6:Effects of interaction length, policy learning and the harness.(1) Timing F1 versus video duration, and Recall in the early versus late half of the trajectory for each Dynamic Intent subtype. (2) Absolute metric changes of SFT over the base model and of RL over SFT. (3) Gains from adding the Harness to the SFT and RL policies across intent categories. Tolerance:τ=2\tau=2s.

Figure 7:Case studies of implicit proactive interaction.Across physical and digital tasks, StreamVibe-VL better aligns response timing and content with the evolving visual evidence and task state, while streaming baselines more often produce premature, missing, or inconsistent assistance.

Figure 8:Category difficulty across StreamVibe-Bench.Each cell gives
the mean score across all models available in that setting; the line spans the
per-model range and the dot marks the median. Outlines identify the lowest
mean within each intent type and metric. Pointwise uses gold interaction history
(n=7n{=}7models), whereas Trajectory uses model-generated interaction history
and also includes native streaming baselines (n=12n{=}12models). All results use
the±2\pm 2s tolerance.

Figure 10:How RL changes the operating point by subtype.Cells report
StreamVibe-VL (RL) minus StreamVibe-VL (SFT) in percentage points under Trajectory evaluation.
Numbers retain the metric’s natural sign; color encodes benefit, so a negativeFPRnear\mathrm{FPR}_{\rm near}change is blue. The visualization jointly exposes
timing, coverage, false interventions, answer quality, and Content-F1.
